Before the plan itself: one element of the brief can't be built as specified in Switzerland, and it's better you hear it from me than from the Rechtsdienst or an appeal court.

**The "no caseworker" part is not legally viable.** A Sozialhilfe-Verfügung must be issued by a natural person vested with decision-making competence under the SHG BE and your Gemeindeordnung. The Federal Supreme Court's 2022 ruling on Basel's fully automated bus-lane dispositions (BGE 148 III 431, case 1C_471/2021) held that even simple, standardized mass decisions require a human decision-maker — fully automated Verfügungen violate rechtliches Gehör (Art. 29 BV) and the duty to give reasons, because the decision isn't attributable to a responsible person. Beyond that: Sozialhilfe decisions require Einzelfallprüfung, often Ermessen (sanktionen, Notbedarf, Mitwirkungsverstösse), the SKOS-Richtlinien expect a personal Rücksprache especially before rejections, and the revised KIG BE imposes GDPR-style safeguards (DPIA, rules on automated individual decisions) on this sensitive-data processing. Please have legal services confirm the details — but I would not bring a fully autonomous version to your Exekutive at all.

The good news: roughly 70–80% of the effort — intake, document processing, calculation, drafting, routing — is fully automatable. The system below is the compliant version: **AI prepares everything; a human decides and signs.** That's where the real time savings are anyway.

## Project plan

| Phase | Duration | Key activities | Gate/deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 – Preparation | 4–6 wks | Clarify decision competences (SHG BE, Gemeindeordnung); legal opinion (Rechtsdienst + kantonale Aufsicht + DSB); define scope (new applications first); KPIs and success criteria | Go/no-go; Lastenheft |
| 1 – Procurement | 2–4 months | Market survey; tender (check IVÖV thresholds early — it changes the route); requirements: CH hosting, Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag, no training on your data, explainability, auditability | Contract, AVV, DPIA v1 |
| 2 – Build & integrate | 3–5 months | Portal intake; OCR/IDP trained on the ~10–15 relevant document types (Lohnausweis, Mietvertrag, Kontoauszüge, KV-Nachweis…); rules engine implementing SHV BE/SKOS (maintained by **Sozialhilfeleitung, not the vendor**); review UI; letter templates incl. Rechtsmittelbelehrung; audit logging; integration with your Fachapplikation | Testable system |
| 3 – Testing & shadow mode | 6–8 wks | AI runs in parallel on past/anonymized cases with no output to applicants; measure extraction accuracy and calculation validity; red-team edge cases; bias checks | Accuracy thresholds met; DPIA finalized |
| 4 – Pilot | 2–3 months | New applications only; caseworkers decide on system-prepared drafts; weekly review board; tune triage thresholds | Pilot report |
| 5 – Rollout | 4–8 wks | Training, fallback procedure, applicant-facing transparency notice; later extend to revisions/budget reviews | Full operation |
| 6 – Operations | ongoing | QA sampling (~10%), KPI dashboard, drift monitoring, annual legal/DPIA review, incident process, vendor SLAs | Governance cycle |

Indicative budget for a mid-sized Gemeinde: CHF 200–500k including integration, heavily dependent on buy-vs-build and your existing Fachapplikation's APIs; licences recur.

## Workflow

**Stage 1 — Intake (fully automated)**
1. Secure upload + identity verification (paper applications digitized on arrival).
2. AI classifies documents, OCRs, extracts fields with confidence scores.
3. Completeness check against the questionnaire checklist.
4. Missing documents → **automated template reminder with deadline** (administrative correspondence, not a Verfügung — this step legitimately runs without any human). Escalate to a caseworker when the deadline lapses.

**Stage 2 — Assessment (AI-prepared)**
5. System builds the case: household composition, income/assets/expenses per SHV/SKOS, computes Bedarf and claim; every figure in the Budget table is linked to its source document.
6. Plausibility and anomaly checks (inconsistencies, asset red flags, prior-case history) → risk score.
7. **Triage:** 🟢 clean first application → one-touch review · 🟡 minor gaps or borderline budget → standard review · 🔴 discrepancies, sanctions, Ermessen, complex households → senior caseworker, AI figures must be re-verified.

**Stage 3 — Decision (human, mandatory)**
8. Caseworker sees one screen: draft Verfügung, calculation, extracted data, source documents, system rationale. Confirms or corrects each material figure; the system logs what was checked and changed.
9. Letter auto-drafted from the approved calculation and legal bases. **No generative free text in calculations or legal reasoning** — deterministic rules for money, templates for text.
10. E-signature by the competent decision-maker; dispatch; archival.

**Stage 4 — Follow-up**
11. Rejections include the Rücksprache offer (a human conversation). Appeals are answered using the logged decision trail.
12. Ongoing casework (revisions, new documents) re-enters the pipeline; QA feeds back into triage thresholds.

## Key safeguards

- Named decision-maker per case; applicants are informed AI supports processing but a human decides.
- Complete audit trail: every AI output, version, and human change.
- CASeworkers must genuinely review, not rubber-stamp: forced field confirmations, override analytics, stratified QA.
- Annual bias audit (nationality, gender, household type); CH hosting; retention per cantonal archiving rules.
- One line for your requirements document: the EU AI Act classifies public-body AI for social benefits as high-risk (Annex III) — Swiss practice will converge there, so write those requirements in now.

## Top risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Decisions overturned on appeal (insufficient human review) | Structured review protocol, full logging, Rechtsdienst approves letter templates |
| Extraction errors → wrong calculation | Confidence thresholds, source-linked figures, mandatory confirmation of key amounts, QA on 100% of calculations |
| LLM hallucination in letters | Templates only, no free text, retrieval-grounded figures |
| Rubber-stamping / deskilling | Forced confirmations, override-rate tracking, QA rotation |
| Discrimination | Bias testing, stratified QA sampling, report to DSB |
| Vendor lock-in | Exit clauses, open export formats, no-training clause |

## KPIs

Median processing days · % one-touch cases · extraction accuracy · calculation error rate at QA · AI override rate · appeal reversal rate · staff hours per case.

## Immediate next steps

1. Brief the Rechtsdienst for a short assessment of the human-decision requirement (BGE 148 III 431) and KIG BE implications.
2. Align with the Sozialhilfeleitung on the role change — the jobs shift from data entry and calculation toward review, decision, and QA, not disappear.
3. Approach the kantonale Aufsichtsbehörde and Datenschutzbeauftragte early; it saves months later.
4. Define scope and KPIs with the department.
5. Run a market survey to test the vendor landscape before committing budget.

Happy to produce a German version of this for the Exekutive, or a one-page decision paper contrasting the (infeasible) autonomous variant with this one.

   Stage 1 – Intake (fully automated):
   1. Upload/identity via secure portal (or digitize paper).

   Stage 2 – Assessment (AI-prepared):
   5. System builds the file: household composition, income/assets/expenses per SKOS/SHV, computes Bedarf, Leistungsanspruch, creates the Budget table with each figure linked to its source document.
   6. Plausibility/anomaly checks (inconsistencies, missing employer info, asset flags, prior-case history), fraud indicators → risk score.
   7. Triage: Green (complete, clean, standard first application) → one-touch review. Yellow (minor gaps, borderline budget) → standard review. Red (discrepancies, sanctions, Ermessen, complex household) → senior caseworker, no reliance on AI draft figures without re-verification.

   8. Caseworker sees one screen: draft Verfügung, calculation, extracted data, source docs, system's rationale. Confirms or corrects each material figure; system logs what was checked and changed.
